pictures.scene: Gerrit van Honthorst, King David Playing the Harp — the king with his head thrown back and his mouth open in song, the spiked gold crown over his striped turban and the ermine and gold brocade mantle on his shoulders, one hand up among the strings of the harp, for the choirmaster to the tune of The Death of the Son, a Psalm of David
pictures.name: pd_honthorst_king_david_playing_the_harp

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Angelus — the peasant woman standing alone in the dug field at dusk with her head bowed and her hands folded, the basket and the barrow left where she was working and the far church spire small on the horizon behind her, I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart, I will recount all Your wonders
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_angelus

pictures.scene: Hans Memling, Christ with Singing Angels — Christ in a jewelled crown and blue mantle raising His hand in blessing against the gold ground, and beside Him two crowned angels in green and brocaded copes singing out of a great open book, clouds under their feet, I will be glad and rejoice in You, I will sing praise to Your name O Most High
pictures.name: pd_memling_singing_angels

pictures.scene: Paolo Uccello, The Battle of San Romano — the white warhorse plunging forward into the press of armoured men with the lances crossing over its head, a rider gone down under its hooves among the broken staves and the empty helmets, a grey horse lying on its side at the bottom and the hares running off over the dark fields behind, when my enemies retreat, they stumble and perish before You
pictures.name: pd_uccello_the_battle_of_san_romano

pictures.scene: Deesis, Hagia Sophia — the great mosaic Christ looking straight out from the broken gold wall, the cross set in the halo behind His head, His hand raised in blessing and the jewelled gospel book held against His blue mantle, the plaster fallen away all round Him, for You have upheld my just cause, You sit on Your throne judging righteously
pictures.name: pd_deesis_pantocrator

pictures.scene: David Roberts, The Siege and Destruction of Jerusalem — the whole city laid out under a smoke-darkened sky, the temple courts still standing white in the middle of it with smoke going up from the walls on either side, the armies pouring in long columns up the valley and along the ravine below the ramparts, a bent palm tree over the ruins in front, You have rebuked the nations, You have destroyed the wicked
pictures.name: pd_roberts_the_siege_and_destruction_of_jerusalem

pictures.scene: Giovanni Paolo Panini, Ruins — the bronze emperor still sitting his horse on a round pedestal above a field of fallen stone, carved blocks and broken column drums lying everywhere on the grass, a few countrymen in cloaks loitering and leaning among them under a wide pale sky, You have erased their name forever and ever, the enemy has come to eternal ruin
pictures.name: pd_panini_ruines

pictures.scene: Louis Daguerre, Ruins of Holyrood Chapel — the roofless chapel by moonlight, the great traceried window standing empty with the open sky behind its mullions, grass and bushes growing out of the broken gable, the aisle arches and the fallen monuments left in the dark below, and You have uprooted their cities, the very memory of them has vanished
pictures.name: pd_daguerre_holyrood_chapel_ruins

pictures.scene: Christ Pantocrator, Cefalu — the vast mosaic Christ filling the gold apse, the cross set in the halo behind His head, one hand raised and the other holding the open book that reads I am the light of the world, and below Him the Virgin standing with her hands lifted between two winged archangels, but the LORD abides forever, He has established His throne for judgment
pictures.name: pd_master_of_cefalu_christ_pantocrator

pictures.scene: Philippe de Champaigne, Moses Presenting the Tablets of the Law — the old prophet in a blue velvet mantle over gold brocade, the two horns of light in his white hair, holding up the great stone tablets with the ten commandments written out on them in numbered lines and looking straight out at us over them, He judges the world with justice, He governs the people with equity
pictures.name: pd_de_champaigne_moses_presenting_the_tablets_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Karl Friedrich Schinkel, Gothic Church on a Rock by the Sea — the great church standing up dark on its wooded crag with all its spires and buttresses against the last light, the water lying below at the foot of the rock and a cross on the parapet above it, the LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble
pictures.name: pd_schinkel_gothic_church_on_a_rock_by_the_sea

pictures.scene: Maurycy Gottlieb, Jews Praying in the Synagogue on Yom Kippur — the crowded synagogue on the fast day, men in striped prayer shawls bowed over the reading desk with their hands pressed to their faces, one carrying the dressed Torah scroll in his arms, a child looking out at us from the front and the women watching down from the gallery above, those who know Your name trust in You, You have not forsaken those who seek You
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Frederic Edwin Church, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the whole city lying along the far ridge behind its long wall with the great dome and the minarets standing up in the evening light, the valley of olives dropping away between, and three small travellers with a camel halted on the stony track in the front, sing praises to the LORD who dwells in Zion, proclaim His deeds among the nations
pictures.name: pd_church_jerusalem_from_the_mount_of_olives

pictures.scene: Eduard Bendemann, Jews Mourning in Exile — the old harper sitting on the ground in his red robe and yellow turban with an iron fetter and chain on his wrist, his hand resting on the silent strings and his face turned away, the young woman beside him fallen against his knee with her head in her arms, for the Avenger of bloodshed remembers, He does not ignore the cry of the afflicted
pictures.name: pd_bendemann_jews_mourning_in_exile

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jeremiah Lamenting — the old prophet sitting alone in the rocks with his head propped on his hand and his eyes down, his grey robe and embroidered coat spread about him, the rescued gold vessels piled at his elbow and the open book under his arm, the burning city throwing its light up behind him, be merciful to me O LORD, see how my enemies afflict me
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jeremiah_lamenting

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Raising of Lazarus — Christ standing over the open grave in the rock with His arm thrown straight up and His face set, the dead man rising out of the tomb in his white grave clothes with his eyes opening, the mourners shrinking back with their hands up and their mouths open, lift me up from the gates of death, that I may declare all Your praises
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_raising_of_lazarus

pictures.scene: Gustav Bauernfeind, The Gate of Jerusalem — the old street climbing to the high stone arch with the lattice windows and the awnings hung over it, the sun coming down the cobbles, the people going up and down through the gateway and a man in a white headcloth walking out towards us with his staff, that within the gates of Daughter Zion I may rejoice in Your salvation
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_gate

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Tower of Babel — the huge tower climbing tier on tier out of the rock it is eating into, the upper storeys still raw red brick with scaffolding and cranes all over them, the arches below already crooked and settling, and the stonecutters working away at their blocks on the grass in the front, the nations have fallen into a pit of their making, their feet are caught in the net they have hidden
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Anthonie van Borssom, Nets by Moonlight — the long line of fishing nets slung on their stakes along the dark bank, one man working at them with his back to us, the moon hanging low behind the sail of a barge and laying its track right across the water to the nets, the LORD is known by the justice He brings, the wicked are ensnared by the work of their hands
pictures.name: pd_borssom_netten

pictures.scene: Pieter Claesz, Vanitas Still Life — the skull laid on the bare table among the crossed bones, the half-empty glass standing beside it, an overturned cup, a clay pipe and the palette with its little smears of paint, all of it left out in the dark, the wicked will return to Sheol, all the nations who forget God
pictures.name: pd_claesz_vanitas_still_life

pictures.scene: John Everett Millais, The Blind Girl — the beggar girl sitting out in the wet meadow with her face lifted to the sun she cannot see, the little paper sign at her neck and the concertina on her lap, the younger child leaning into her shoulder and looking back at the double rainbow standing over the village, for the needy will not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the oppressed forever dashed
pictures.name: pd_millais_the_blind_girl

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Christ in Glory — Christ seated inside the great blue mandorla on a gold ground with His hand raised in judgment, the little ringed heads of the angels set all round the rim, the saints and the Virgin kneeling to either side and an angel below holding up the cross, rise up O LORD do not let man prevail, let the nations be judged in Your presence
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_christ_in_glory

pictures.scene: Frans Hals, Young Man with a Skull — the boy in a red cap with a great pink plume and a cloak thrown over his shoulder, turning to speak to us with his hand raised, holding a bare skull up in his other hand, lay terror upon them O LORD, let the nations know they are but men
pictures.name: pd_hals_young_man_with_a_skull

lines.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Death of the Son.”
A Psalm of David.
I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart;
I will recount all Your wonders.
I will be glad and rejoice in You;
I will sing praise to Your name, O Most High.
When my enemies retreat,
they stumble and perish before You.
For You have upheld my just cause;
You sit on Your throne judging righteously.
You have rebuked the nations;
You have destroyed the wicked;
You have erased their name forever and ever.
The enemy has come to eternal ruin,
and You have uprooted their cities;
the very memory of them has vanished.
But the LORD abides forever;
He has established His throne for judgment.
He judges the world with justice;
He governs the people with equity.
The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed,
a stronghold in times of trouble.
Those who know Your name trust in You,
for You, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.
Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion;
proclaim His deeds among the nations.
For the Avenger of bloodshed remembers;
He does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.
Be merciful to me, O LORD;
see how my enemies afflict me!
Lift me up from the gates of death,
that I may declare all Your praises—
that within the gates of Daughter Zion
I may rejoice in Your salvation.
The nations have fallen into a pit of their making;
their feet are caught in the net they have hidden.
The LORD is known by the justice He brings;
the wicked are ensnared by the work of their hands.
The wicked will return to Sheol—
all the nations who forget God.
For the needy will not always be forgotten;
nor the hope of the oppressed forever dashed.
Rise up, O LORD, do not let man prevail;
let the nations be judged in Your presence.
Lay terror upon them, O LORD;
let the nations know they are but men.
